rows.meaning: Spatial dimension, $d \in \{1, 2, 3\}$.
Exponent in the spatial covariance homogeneity relation.
Temporal covariance exponent; $a = \alpha_0$ in the integrated arguments.
Spatial covariance measure; $\gamma$ denotes its density when one exists and otherwise the corresponding distribution.
Spectral measure, in the Fourier convention fixed by the hypothesis.
Gaussian forcing and its isonormal realization on covariance test classes, respectively.
Expectation under the underlying probability measure.
Normalization exponent $(4 - \alpha - \alpha_0)/(3 - \alpha)$ in the moment bounds and limit.
In the interval-field estimates, $\beta = 4 - \alpha - \alpha_0$ and $\nu = 3 - \alpha$. These letters have different local uses in path estimates.
Spectral-mass constant in the independent upper bound.
Euler Gamma and Beta functions; $\Gamma_E$ is distinct from the covariance measure $\Gamma$.
Degree of an auxiliary static covariance in the comparison arguments; it need not equal $\alpha$.
Canonical Stratonovich solution with displacement $1$ and velocity $0$ at time zero.
Wave Green measure, with mass $t$ and support in the closed radius-$t$ ball.
Ordered chain kernel and its multiple Stratonovich integral.
The $n$th Stratonovich term $S_n(g_n)$; its iteration order is not an orthogonal chaos order.
The two ordered chains and the pair partitions of their $2k$ vertices.
Number of pair partitions, $(2k)!/(2^k k!)$.
Pairing integral for chain lengths $m,n$ and pair partition $D$.
Laplace-damped wave norms used in the construction estimates.
Numerical majorant obtained by estimating each pairing separately; it is not the actual second moment.
Completion of smooth positive-time tests modulo covariance-null tests for the original noise.
The unit time interval; control tests have support in $(0,1)$, while compact parameter families also use $[0,1]$.
Temporal and spatial covariance Hilbert spaces.
Covariance space of tests supported in $I \times \mathbb{R}^d$, embedded in $H_W$.
Bessel multiplier $(1-\Delta)^{1/2}$.
Wave phase $E_r = H^r \times H^{r-1}$; the balanced phase is $E = H^{1/2} \times H^{-1/2}$.
Extended phase $F = E \oplus \mathbb{R}^2$ and the vector encoding constant initial displacement.
Free wave groups on the respective phase spaces.
Integrated Gaussian interaction operator path with spatial localization radius $R$.
Young evolution driven by an operator path $D$ in the interaction representation.
Physical wave evolution obtained by conjugating the interaction flow by the free wave group.
Potential insertion $(u,v) \mapsto (0,Vu)$ on $E$.
Symplectic form and its representing skew-adjoint operator on $E$.

title: Regularization, spatial masks and time blocks

rows.meaning: Gaussian heat kernel used for spatial smoothing; its covariance normalization is specified locally.
A pair of noise-smoothing widths and the corresponding regularized source. In damped phase estimates, $\rho$ instead denotes a positive damping parameter.
Spatial radius, cutoff profile and physical mask. In the uniform-radius arguments, $\eta_R = \eta(\cdot/R)$ and $m_R = \eta_R^2$.
Long-time normalization $\delta = T^{-\kappa}$ and shrinking spatial scale $r_T = T\delta$. Smoothing parameters denoted by $\delta$ elsewhere are local.
Fast-noise amplitude $\delta^{(1 - a)/2}$.
Fast block length, number of full blocks, slow block starts and final block length. Here $\tau \in [0,B)$.
Isometry used to pull each fast-time test back to the original Gaussian noise.
Random block operator input and its deterministic mean shift; these local symbols differ from the Stratonovich terms $X_n(t,x)$.
Growing spatial radius $\delta^{-1} + 2$ in the point upper bound; it differs from the shrinking scale $r_T$.
Auxiliary spatial and temporal regularity exponents. Here $\gamma$ is not the covariance distribution and $\beta$ is not the coefficient-growth exponent.
Nonzero nonnegative smooth compact spacetime controls; separation into time and space factors is not required.
Deterministic covariance mean induced by the control $\Psi$.
Original Gaussian variance, equal to the squared covariance-space norm of the control.
Positive Rayleigh growth rate and its integral over the unit interval, for nonzero covariance.
Squared Rayleigh rate used in the introductory constant formula.
Supremum of $cI_\Psi - v_\Psi/2$. The coefficient-one value is auxiliary; the coefficient-two value identifies $C_2$.
Intrinsic second-moment constant, including its zero-covariance value.
In the spatial-energy and constant calculations, $k = 3 - \alpha$, $q = 4 - \alpha$ and $m = q/k$. These are local conventions.
Temporal equilibrium density and its total mass. $M_a$ is distinct from the mean-growth rate $M(a)$.
Original temporal kernel $|s-t|^{-a}$ and its maximal row integral $2^a/(1 - a)$.
Physical two-point covariance pairing.
Spatial covariance energy of $f^2$ and gradient energy $\|\nabla f\|_2^2$.
Best homogeneous spatial energy ratio, extended to real unit $H^1$ profiles.
Supremum of $A_{\mathrm{sp}}(f) - b(f)/2$ over unit spatial profiles.
Scalar map from spatial energy to a variational bound; it is distinct from the wave phase $F$.
Admissible time-dependent unit spatial profiles and their integrated gradient energy.
Original temporal occupation energy and its homogeneous ratio supremum.
Occupation energy with gradient penalty $\zeta T(g)$, using the original temporal kernel.
Auxiliary damped temporal kernel and its occupation energy; these differ from the original-kernel quantities.
Temporal, spatial and combined covariance-mean maps. Their domains and radius dependence are specified at each construction.
Signed-control variational value at radius $R$ and its limsup along the growing radii.
Compact operators on the Hilbert phase $E$.
Banach space of block paths with its weighted temporal norm.
In Gaussian enlargement, $Ch = \mathbb{E}[XW(h)] = \sqrt\delta\,\mathcal{M}_\delta h$. The letter $C$ elsewhere often denotes an estimate constant.
Visible isonormal subspace and Cameron--Martin image of the covariance map.
Closed support space of the Gaussian input; this is distinct from the wave phase $E$.
Expected squared operator norm of the physical endpoint in the upper argument.
Finite Gram matrix entries $\langle k_i,k_j\rangle$, assumed nonnegative in the positive-cone optimization.
Finite-control objective and its supremum.
Dual objective and its infimum for a selected subset $A$. The empty subset has value zero.
Positive dual minimizer and the corresponding positive combination of Gram vectors.

title: Static comparisons and local outlook notation

rows.meaning: Static first-mean rate and static time exponent; the comparison retains the source normalization stated there.
Normalized first-mean limsup in the near-static comparison; it is not the equilibrium mass $M_a$.
In the clock comparison only, correlation of the two auxiliary Brownian clocks; neither a source width nor a damping parameter.
In future-work moment statements, a fixed moment order. Elsewhere it may be an auxiliary integrability or Schatten index.
Locally, $p = 2 - \alpha_0$ in the interval-field argument, while $\nu = 1/\theta$ in Young growth estimates.
In the conditional upper-tail discussion, $A = 2^{-m}C_2$ and $z_* = mA$. This $A$ is not the occupation energy $A(g)$.
Conditional upper-tail rate on the stated range of thresholds.
Covariance Hilbert space for the spatial-white optimizer conjecture.
Control objective and spatial translation in the optimizer conjecture.
In the smooth logarithmic-wave outlook, $h = \log|u|$ and $h = b(t)+\varphi$. This $b(t)$ is distinct from the spatial energy $b(f)$.
